_comment: Technical notes per check for the Claude Code export (English). fix = what to change, verify = how to confirm it, effort = quick | moderate | larger. Client-facing wording lives in texts.json.

basics.https.fix: Install a TLS certificate (Let's Encrypt or the host's free certificate), serve every page over https and update hard-coded http:// links, canonical tags and the CMS site URL (WordPress: Settings → General, or WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL).
basics.https.verify: Open https://<domain>/ without a browser warning; `curl -sI https://<domain>/` returns 200.

basics.ssl_valid.fix: Renew or replace the certificate so it is valid, not expired, issued for this hostname (including or excluding www as used) and served with the full intermediate chain.
basics.ssl_valid.verify: `openssl s_client -connect <domain>:443 -servername <domain>` shows `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`; SSL Labs grade A or B.

basics.http_redirect.fix: Redirect every http:// request to the same path on https:// with a 301 (server config, .htaccess `RewriteRule` or the hosting panel's 'force HTTPS'). Consider an HSTS header afterwards.

mobile.viewport.fix: Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` to <head>; remove user-scalable=no / maximum-scale=1 so people can zoom. Without a responsive stylesheet this alone is not enough (see the other mobile problems).
mobile.viewport.verify: The tag is present in page/source.html; on a 390px-wide phone view text is readable without zooming.

mobile.font_size.fix: Set a base font size of at least 16px for body text on small screens and use relative units (rem) for text; check footer, captions and menu text, which are often set in 10–12px.
mobile.font_size.verify: In a 390px viewport no running text is smaller than 12px (DevTools → computed font-size).

mobile.tap_targets.fix: Make links and buttons at least 44×44px on phones (48px is better; use padding or min-height) or add at least 8px space between them. The 'Where' list names the elements that are too small or too close.
mobile.tap_targets.verify: Re-run the audit, or check the listed selectors in a 390px viewport: each target's box is ≥ 44px or clearly separated.

mobile.horizontal_scroll.fix: Find the elements wider than the screen (listed under 'Where') and constrain them: `max-width: 100%` for images/iframes/tables, avoid fixed pixel widths, wrap long words or URLs, use responsive layouts (flex/grid) instead of fixed-width containers.

speed.pagespeed_mobile.fix: Work through the largest PageSpeed opportunities: compress and resize images, defer non-critical JavaScript, remove unused CSS/JS and plugins, enable caching and compression on the server.
speed.pagespeed_mobile.verify: Run PageSpeed Insights for mobile again and compare the performance score.

speed.pagespeed_desktop.fix: Same levers as mobile: smaller images, less render-blocking JavaScript and CSS, server caching and compression.
speed.pagespeed_desktop.verify: Run PageSpeed Insights for desktop again and compare the performance score.

speed.core_web_vitals.fix: LCP: serve the main hero image small and early (preload, no lazy-loading above the fold). TBT/INP: cut and defer JavaScript. CLS: give images and embeds width/height or aspect-ratio and avoid inserting content above existing content.
speed.core_web_vitals.verify: PageSpeed Insights or Lighthouse shows LCP, TBT/INP and CLS in the green range.

speed.large_images.fix: Resize the listed images to at most about twice their displayed width, convert photos to WebP/AVIF (or well-compressed JPEG), and use srcset/sizes so phones load smaller versions.
speed.large_images.verify: The listed files are each under 300 KB and not much wider than displayed (Network tab or re-run the audit).

speed.page_weight.fix: Reduce what the homepage downloads: optimise images first, then remove unused fonts, sliders, tracking scripts and plugins. See PAGE.md → assets for the requests by type.
speed.page_weight.verify: DevTools Network panel shows the total transfer for the homepage clearly lower than before.

speed.server_response.fix: Enable page caching (CMS cache plugin or server cache), use a current PHP/runtime version, check slow database queries or plugins; consider better hosting or a CDN.
speed.server_response.verify: `curl -o /dev/null -s -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' https://<domain>/` stays below about 0.8 s over several tries.

seo.title.fix: Write a unique <title> of about 30–60 characters: main service + town + business name (e.g. 'Kaderníctvo v Trnave – Salón Lena'). Avoid generic titles like 'Home' or 'Úvod'.
seo.title.verify: The new <title> appears in page/source.html after deploying and in the browser tab.

seo.canonical.fix: Make the homepage's `<link rel="canonical">` point at its own final URL (https + the host the site actually serves, trailing slash included), or drop the tag so the CMS stops copying a template value.
seo.canonical.verify: `curl -s https://<domain>/ | grep canonical` shows the homepage's own address, and Search Console reports the homepage as the canonical.

seo.thin_content.fix: Write real body copy for the homepage: what the business does, for whom, where, and what to do next. Aim past 250 visible words, not with filler but with the questions customers actually ask.
seo.thin_content.verify: The rendered page (not just the HTML source) carries the text; re-running the scan reports more words.

seo.meta_description.fix: Add `<meta name="description">` with about 70–160 characters describing what the business offers and where; make it read like an invitation to click.
seo.meta_description.verify: The tag is present in the server HTML with a sensible length.

seo.h1.fix: Use exactly one <h1> per page that states what the page is about; turn other big headings into <h2>/<h3>. Don't put the logo image alone in the H1 without text.

seo.indexable.fix: Remove `noindex` from the robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header and make sure robots.txt does not block the whole site (WordPress: Settings → Reading → 'Discourage search engines' off).
seo.indexable.verify: No noindex in page/source.html or the response headers; robots.txt allows `/`.

seo.sitemap.fix: Publish an XML sitemap (most CMSs or SEO plugins generate one, e.g. /wp-sitemap.xml) and reference it in robots.txt with `Sitemap: https://<domain>/sitemap.xml`.
seo.sitemap.verify: The sitemap URL returns XML with <urlset> or <sitemapindex>.

seo.open_graph.fix: Add og:title, og:description and og:image (at least 1200×630px) meta tags so shared links show a proper preview.
seo.open_graph.verify: The tags are in the server HTML; a link preview (e.g. Facebook Sharing Debugger) shows the image and text.

seo.favicon.fix: Add a favicon: `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">` plus a PNG/ICO fallback and an apple-touch-icon (180×180).
seo.favicon.verify: The icon appears in the browser tab and /favicon.ico or the linked file returns 200.

seo.structured_data.fix: Add JSON-LD for the business (schema.org LocalBusiness or a specific type such as HairSalon/AutoRepair) with name, address, opening hours and URL. Ask the user for the phone number instead of inventing one.
seo.structured_data.verify: Google's Rich Results Test or validator.schema.org reads the block without errors.

trust.contact.fix: Show the phone number and e-mail visibly on the homepage (header or footer) and on a contact page. The real values were removed from this export; ask the user for them.
trust.contact.verify: A visitor can see a phone number or e-mail on the homepage without scrolling through several screens.

trust.clickable_phone.fix: Wrap phone numbers in `<a href="tel:+421...">` links (international format, no spaces in the href) so phones can call with one tap. Ask the user for the number.
trust.clickable_phone.verify: Every visible phone number on the homepage is inside a tel: link.

trust.address_map.fix: Show the street address (ideally in an <address> element) and a map or a link to Google Maps / Mapy.cz on the homepage or contact page.
trust.address_map.verify: Address text and a map embed or map link are present.

trust.footer_year.fix: Update the © year in the footer, preferably generated automatically (PHP `date('Y')`, a template variable or JavaScript).
trust.footer_year.verify: The footer shows the current year.

trust.social_links.fix: Point social icons to the business's actual profile pages (not facebook.com/ or a theme demo) or remove icons for networks the business doesn't use.
trust.social_links.verify: Each social link opens the business's own profile.

trust.cookie_banner.fix: Load analytics/marketing scripts only after consent: add a consent banner (CMP) or remove the trackers. With Google Analytics use Consent Mode; don't fire tags before the visitor accepts.
trust.cookie_banner.verify: In a fresh private window, no requests to tracking hosts happen before clicking 'Accept'.

trust.broken_links.fix: Fix or remove the listed links (each shows the target, the HTTP result and the element that links to it); redirect deleted pages with 301 to the closest current page.
trust.broken_links.verify: Each listed URL returns 200 (or the link is gone).

tech.cms_version.fix: Back up the site, then update the CMS core, theme and plugins to current versions; remove unused plugins. Hide the version number from the generator meta tag if possible.
tech.cms_version.verify: The CMS admin shows no pending core updates; the generator tag no longer shows an old version.

tech.outdated_libraries.fix: Upgrade the listed libraries (e.g. jQuery to 3.x with jQuery Migrate during the transition) or remove them if unused; test sliders, menus and forms afterwards.
tech.outdated_libraries.verify: `jQuery.fn.jquery` (or the library's version) in the console shows the new version; no new console errors.

tech.console_errors.fix: Open the browser console on the homepage and fix the listed errors: missing files (404s), scripts loaded in the wrong order, calls to removed APIs.
tech.console_errors.verify: Console shows no red errors after a full page load (desktop and mobile).

tech.mixed_content.fix: Change the listed http:// resources to https:// (or protocol-relative/relative URLs); in a CMS run a search-and-replace on the database for the old http URL.
tech.mixed_content.verify: Browser console shows no 'Mixed Content' warnings; all resources load over https.

a11y.contrast.fix: Darken text or lighten backgrounds for the listed elements to reach WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (24px+, or 18.66px+ bold). Adjust the theme colour variables rather than single elements when possible.
a11y.contrast.verify: A contrast checker (DevTools colour picker) shows ≥ 4.5:1 for each listed element.

a11y.img_alt.fix: Add meaningful alt text to the listed images (what the image shows or does); use alt="" for purely decorative images.
a11y.img_alt.verify: Every has an alt attribute; informative images have a description.

a11y.form_labels.fix: Give each listed field a visible <label for="id"> (placeholder text alone disappears while typing and is not a label); use aria-label only when a visible label is impossible.
a11y.form_labels.verify: Clicking each label focuses its field; no field relies on placeholder alone.

a11y.control_names.fix: Give icon-only links and buttons an accessible name: visible text, aria-label, or alt text on the icon image (e.g. aria-label="Facebook").
a11y.control_names.verify: In DevTools → Accessibility each listed element has a non-empty name.

a11y.lang.fix: Declare the page language on the root element, e.g. `<html lang="sk">` (cs, en …).

design.fixed_width.fix: Replace fixed-width containers (the listed elements) with fluid layouts: max-width + width:100%, flex/grid, media queries. Old table or 960px layouts usually need a responsive rebuild of the template.
design.fixed_width.verify: At a 700px-wide window there is no horizontal scrollbar and content reflows.

design.table_layout.fix: Rebuild the listed layout tables with semantic elements (header, nav, main, section, footer) and CSS grid/flex; keep <table> only for tabular data.
design.table_layout.verify: No <table> is used for page structure; the page still reads correctly at phone width.

design.small_text.fix: Raise the base font size to 16px and avoid text below 14px on desktop, especially for paragraphs, menu items and footer text.
design.small_text.verify: Computed font-size of body text is ≥ 16px; no running text below 14px.

design.font_count.fix: Limit the design to one or two font families (one for headings, one for text) and remove unused webfont loads.
design.font_count.verify: PAGE.md → assets → fonts lists at most two text families after the change.

design.legacy_markup.fix: Replace the listed obsolete elements (<font>, <center>, <marquee>, Flash, body bgcolor…) with CSS and modern HTML; remove Flash content entirely.
design.legacy_markup.verify: None of the listed tags remain in page/source.html.

design_ai.review.fix: Address the design review points (layout, hierarchy, imagery, consistency). Show the user a proposal before restyling.
design_ai.review.verify: Compare new screenshots with screenshots/desktop.jpg and screenshots/mobile.jpg.
